about.bio: Frontend developer since 2018 — first at a <hugeCorporation>large e-commerce SaaS</hugeCorporation>, then a <agency>product studio</agency>, then US product startups. Day to day I work on data-heavy interfaces — dashboards, complex tables, multi-step flows — and the refactors that keep them fast as they grow. I like readable code, small reviewable PRs, and working closely with design and product.
about.ai: Since 2024 my daily workflow is built around AI coding agents — mainly Claude Code: project rules and skills, subagents for code review and audits, browser and Playwright MCP for checking the result in a real browser. AI writes the routine — migrations, tests, boilerplate; I keep the architecture, review every diff, and nothing ships without typecheck, tests, and a screenshot.
about.looking: Open to Senior or Lead Frontend roles, remote. I do my best work on products with real UI complexity and a team that values performance and craft — SaaS, fintech, anything with hard frontend problems. English and Russian.

helium10.position: Frontend Developer · US SaaS for Amazon sellers
description: Built Adtomic — Amazon advertising automation: sellers manage campaigns, bids, pricing, and competitor tracking in one place instead of spreadsheets.
Built an internal UI library (a few dozen components) reused by 4+ teams.
Built data-heavy dashboards: tables with thousands of rows, charts, and real-time bid updates over live Amazon data.
Joined a product before launch and took it to production.
Built a no-code page builder in the admin (sliders, carousels, event grids) — marketing ships landing pages in hours instead of days, without a developer.
Sped up page loads by ~30% through caching and rebalancing work between server and client.
Extracted shared components into packages reused across 3–4 studio projects; added accessibility (high-contrast themes, font-size controls); mentored juniors and ran code reviews.
Lead the frontend of two products: Tourseta (tour-operator booking platform, 130+ pages, team of 5–8) and Readyhubb (services marketplace).
Tourseta: public booking site plus operator dashboards — tours, bookings, invoices, payments. Next.js/React on the frontend, shared packages for UI, bookings, money, and i18n in a monorepo.

Frontend is my main focus, but I also take backend tasks (~30% of the time): NestJS + Prisma on PostgreSQL, AWS (S3, SQS, Lambda for file processing and PDF rendering), JWT auth with roles, Swagger, Sentry, Docker.
Added payments (Stripe, Airwallex), PDF generation (invoices, vouchers), transactional email (SendGrid + react-email), and multi-currency / multi-language support end to end.
Optimized load speed — noticeably faster on the slow connections some operators use.
Readyhubb: built the admin and dashboards with no-code content management, so the team launches campaigns on its own.

schoolbusmanager.position: Senior Frontend Engineer · School bus SaaS
description: Led the frontend of a school-bus operations product (routes, schedules, bus and driver tracking): admin app, parent portal, and the company website.

Refactored an old, hard-to-maintain codebase incrementally without pausing production: upgraded React, moved class components to functional, Webpack → Vite (dev rebuilds ~12s → near-instant), server state → TanStack Query, TypeScript across the codebase.
Rebuilt the company website from scratch on Next.js — SSR, server-side data fetching, SEO — and shipped it to production.
Result: heaviest screens load up to ~7× faster, fewer bugs; set up project structure, code style, linters, and automated checks for the team.
Led 4 of 11 packages in a Turborepo monorepo (team of ~15): Projects, Pages, Flow, and Meet (LiveKit video).
Shipped 15+ product features — from sprints and kanban to a project-creation wizard.
Made heavy screens (task lists, kanban) ~2× faster — virtualization, memoization, fewer re-renders.
Mobile adaptivity of key screens; unified i18n for shared components (Mantine 8, i18next). Stack: React 18, Vite, Zustand, Redux Toolkit, TanStack Query.

items.schoolbusmanager: Bus operations SaaS for US school districts — three apps: admin panel (main product), parent app, and the marketing landing I built from scratch. Led a major frontend refactor — migrated Webpack → Vite, Redux → RTK Query, adopted FSD. Up to 7× perf gains on critical screens.
items.tourseta: Multi-tenant SaaS for tour operators — booking flow and per-operator admin. Own the frontend in a team of 5–8, plus ~30% backend on NestJS + Prisma. Next.js monorepo, Radix UI, TanStack Query, Stripe/Airwallex payments, NextAuth, FeatureHub.
items.layers: Work-management platform — pages with databases, projects (tasks/sprints/kanban), visual automations (Flow), in-app video on LiveKit (Meet), and CRM. Team of ~15 engineers. Web + desktop (JAR) builds. React 18 + Vite + Mantine + TanStack Query.

cv.summary: Frontend engineer with 7+ years in React, TypeScript, and Next.js. I like complex product interfaces — dashboards, tables, editors — and I'm good at making slow apps fast and bringing old codebases up to date. Right now I lead the frontend of Tourseta, a booking platform for tour operators, and cover part of its NestJS backend (~30% of my time). I work with AI coding agents daily (Claude Code) and know how to make that workflow reliable in a team. Open to Senior or Lead roles, remote.
